description:
About the Position

Radboud University invites applications for a PhD position on multisynaptic plasticity in dendrites, based in the Donders Institute for Brain, Cognition and Behaviour. The project investigates how plasticity spreads across multiple synaptic sites on dendrites of hippocampal CA1 neurons, using advanced optical techniques including two-photon glutamate uncaging and genetically encoded biosensors. Understanding these dendritic computation rules is central to explaining how the hippocampus stores and retrieves memories.

The position is a salaried four-year doctoral appointment under the Dutch CAO-NU collective agreement. The doctoral candidate will combine two-photon imaging and uncaging experiments in acute brain slices with electrophysiology, biosensor measurements and quantitative analysis of synaptic integration. The supervising group offers state-of-the-art microscopy infrastructure, close day-to-day supervision and a collaborative environment spanning cellular neuroscience and computational modelling.

Candidate Profile

Applicants hold a master's degree in neuroscience, biology, biophysics or a related field, with hands-on laboratory experience and a drive for technically demanding experiments. Experience with patch-clamp electrophysiology, imaging or Python/MATLAB-based data analysis is an advantage. Applications are submitted through Radboud University's recruitment system with a CV, transcripts, references and a motivation letter; interviews include a discussion of the candidate's research experience.

Highlights

  • Salaried four-year PhD in cellular neuroscience at the Donders Institute
  • Two-photon glutamate uncaging in hippocampal CA1
  • Genetically encoded biosensors and electrophysiology
  • Dendritic computation and multisynaptic plasticity
  • State-of-the-art microscopy infrastructure
  • Application via Radboud University's recruitment system
